The module-slice note keeps the starter sample, loader scaffold, and bounded tests reviewable in one Phase 9 packet.
The dedicated survey gate fails closed when the manifest, note, loader scaffold, or ownership packet drifts.
The shared Phase 9 build bundle keeps the trace-events packet wired beside the other runtime pilot surfaces.

Tracks the bounded starter sample, loader scaffold, and directly coupled tests without widening into runtime implementation.

gaps.why_now: The existing Phase 9 build step is the smallest honest place to widen runtime pilot coverage from atomic64 and bitmap into the trace-events starter lane.
A trace-events survey gate keeps the Linux sample anchor, landed starter status, the bounded loader scaffold, and the remaining runtime-substrate blocker explicit while the pilot surface stays small.
A sample-backed lifecycle starter is the first honest runtime-facing trace-events step that can model event emission and callback registration without pretending full macro or thread parity exists.
The Phase 9 roadmap explicitly calls for selftest hooks, and the bounded runtime_trace_events sample already keeps that requirement reviewable through descriptor metadata plus runSelftest().
A dedicated Phase 9 test file keeps the starter sample reviewable and bounded around lifecycle transitions, event emission counts, and registration balance.
A narrow differential gate now captures a few foo_bar, template, and function-callback expectations from the Linux sample before any broader runtime substrate work.

A bounded sample-side loader scaffold now makes the existing requires_runtime_substrate contract reviewable through explicit tracepoint register and unregister APIs, prepared and initialized-stage handoff snapshots that stay stable even if later sample replay mutates local counters, a shared-request bridge through the runtime-loader contract, and a no-substrate release path without pretending a real runtime loader already exists.
A real loadable module entry point, thread creation parity, and tracepoint registration lifecycle still depend on shared runtime substrate pieces that the repo has not started yet.
